messages:
sam: Quick sync: we discovered header-normalization divergence between router v3.4.1 and runtime v2.9.2 during a morning integration smoke. Can we decide pin vs mitigation for the 02:00 UTC change window? @anya @jon
anya: Summary from smoke: routing keys shifted for a small % of requests when prefix caching hit. No functional failures, but p95 latency jumped ~120ms for those flows.
jon: Do we know if console metric names are impacted? I want to avoid alert churn mid-window.
console-bot: Dashboard check: metric aliasing rule 'router.headers.incoming' -> 'router.header.count' mismatch detected in staging. Affected panels: /dash/infra/route-headers, /dash/user/latency.
sam: Thanks. Two options on the table: A) Pin router to v3.4.0 for tonight's window; B) Proceed with 3.4.1 but add conservative traffic ramp and circuit-breaker tuning (lowered request timeout to 1.2s) + stricter canary.
anya: If we choose B we need strong rollback automation. The change interacts with KV cache eviction behavior in runtime; that was tweaked in v2.9.2.
sre-oncall: My concern with B is tail latency risk during peak. However pinning creates a mismatch from our intended rolling plan. If we pin, we should document follow-up steps and a re-roll plan.
deploybot: Preflight checks initiated for change window 1766143210 (2026-03-24T02:00:00Z). Services: api, runtime, console, router. Running smoke and canary sim.
deploybot: Preflight summary:
``napi: OK
runtime v2.9.2: WARN - kv_eviction_rate higher than baseline by 0.7x
console: WARN - metric alias mismatch (see panels)
router v3.4.1: OK
canary-sim @0.5% -> 200 OK, 3x 499, 1x 408 over 5m
```
Observation: transient client timeouts and 499s correlate with kv_eviction spikes. Recommend defensive plan.
jon: Can we run a focused sim where we disable prefix caching to confirm root cause?
anya: Good idea. I'll schedule a short sim and post logs.
sam: Meanwhile suggest we do a temporary pin to v3.4.0 for tonight, and set the canary rollback rules: auto-rollback if error_rate >= 0.8% over 5m OR p99 latency +250ms vs baseline for 5m OR >2 client timeouts in 5m for canary traffic. Manual rollbacks allowed for SEV-level incidents.
sre-oncall: I'll codify those triggers into deploybot and set an on-call watch. Also will prepare quick rollback playbook: command lines, owners, and TL;DR.
deploybot: Applying requested pin: executing pin command and scheduling for 2026-03-24T02:00:00Z.
deploybot: Pin command:
``n./deployctl pin service=router variant=v3.4.0 --window=2026-03-24T02:00:00Z --owner=sam --note="temp pin to match runtime kv behavior"
```
console-bot: Will create a short dashboard shim mapping so metric panels don't break during pin. Also adding a note to release notes about the temporary mismatch.
anya: I've kicked off the cache-disabled sim. Early logs show fewer 499s, which points to eviction interplay. Will confirm after full run.
jon: Action items: 1) sam to apply pin via deploybot (done), 2) sre-oncall to create rollback triggers and watches, 3) anya to finish focused sim and open RW-3499 with kernel tuning plan, 4) console-bot to add metric shim and release note blurb.
sam: Thumbs-up from me if everyone's aligned. Please react with :thumbsup: or raise concerns now.
jon: :thumbsup:
anya: :thumbsup:
sre-oncall: +1
console-bot: :thumbsup:
sam: Pin scheduled and preflight recorded. Follow-up ticket RW-3499 created for post-window roll-forward and kv tuning. Will brief product and infra later. Thanks team.
